source.snippet: KGPG (and, I believe, Kleopatra) provide an interface that allows me to conveniently sign arbitrary text with an enumerated PGP key. Does anything provide this for ssh-keygen -Y sign? I ask due to what community.bitwarden.com describes: Bitwarden supports storing and providing SSH keys. I store my SSH keys inside Bitwarden. Bitwarden does not support PGP.

problem_statement: Security-conscious professionals who store SSH keys in Bitwarden (instead of PGP keys) have no graphical tool to sign arbitrary text with their SSH keys, leaving a usability gap for identity verification and signing workflows that KGPG/Kleopatra fill for PGP.
target_segment: Security engineers, developers, and IT professionals using Bitwarden for SSH key management who need GUI-based SSH signing
notes: Single post but describes a genuine tooling gap created by the intersection of two growing trends: Bitwarden's SSH key support (new) and the shift away from PGP toward SSH for signing. The user is clearly a professional (using Bitwarden for key management, referencing GitLab API key endpoints). A paid GUI utility or Bitwarden-integrated signing tool could find buyers among this segment. Niche but well-defined.
